Subject: Priv deployment licensing boundary & evidence we need

Diego,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited about the private deployment option. Our legal and security teams are reviewing the MSA and want to scope a short addendum that clarifies the permitted license use and what evidence we can ask for during an audit or runbook witness. High-level asks from Orbis: 

- A short, explicit statement of the licensed environment boundary (sites/nodes, DR lanes).
- What operator access the vendor will retain and how operator credentials are handed back at termination.
- A list of acceptable evidence during an audit (forensic snapshot, console logs, witness runbook).
- A timeline for producing artifacts (e.g., 7 business days after request).

Can you share a draft addendum we can circulate with our counsel? Also copy any internal folks who should weigh in (ops/legal).

Best,
Susan
Susan Lewis
Head of IT Procurement
Orbis Health

Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv deployment licensing boundary & evidence we need

Susan — thanks, this is helpful. I pushed a first-pass addendum and an evidence-runbook matrix; both attached. Key notes up front: 

- License boundary: we propose licensed-use is limited to Customer-managed VPCs and specified on-prem hostnames in Exhibit A; any snapshot or image transferred for continuity is strictly for restoration/testing under contracted duties.
- Operator access: Redwood will not retain continuous operator console access in production by default. We allow ephemeral operator sessions for escalations that require mutual-authenticated bastion access; those sessions will be logged and timeboxed.
- Evidence: acceptable items include encrypted forensic snapshots, access logs, KMS audit entries, and an appointed witness test where both parties run a pre-agreed procedure.
- Timing: Redwood can turn around most artifacts within 7 business days; for full forensic snapshots we generally request up to 10 business days to coordinate operator windows.

I flagged a few areas for legal input (see comments in the Word draft): handback of KMS-wrapped key material, limitations on data redelivery, and an operator escalation carveout. Marcus / Lauren / Kimberly — can you scan and suggest quick edits?

Thanks,
Diego
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: PrivDeploy_Addendum_v1.docx (draft addendum), Runbook-Evidence-Matrix.pdf (matrix)

Subject: Re: Priv deployment licensing boundary & evidence we need

Susan, Diego — reviewed the draft. High-level legal edits below (inline comments in the doc as well):

1) Narrow "licensed-use" language to avoid implied redistribution rights — replace "transfer" with "temporary transfer for continuity under strict conditions".
2) KMS/key handback: propose language that requires Redwood to escrow an encrypted key envelope with customer-specific KMS metadata; Redwood never holds the plaintext key post-handover.
3) Audit window: reduce the standard full-snapshot turnaround to 10 business days (we are okay with Orbis asking for expedited access with commercial fees for <5 business days).

We should also add a short paragraph addressing collateralized third-party auditors (i.e., a mutually agreed external auditor). If you want, Diego and I can jump on a short call to resolve the key custody sentence — that is the primary negotiation friction point.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Queueing from an engineering perspective — couple of practical points to add to the runbook: 

- Forensic snapshot policy: snapshots are produced from a stopped-consistent checkpoint to avoid corruption; we need a 4-hour maintenance window for the capture (we can do outside business hours).
- Redaction: customer PII should be redacted when possible before sharing test artifacts; where redaction is not possible we will provide access in a secured review session.
- Witness test: propose a short pre-approved checklist (we added a draft checklist to the Runbook PDF) so both sides know what telemetry and steps will be validated.

I also called out that any request for "console-level" continuous monitoring is not something we agree to in the addendum — ephemeral access only, and only with mutual approval.

Marcus
Senior Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference

Diego/Team — appreciate the quick turnaround and the draft addendum. A few follow-ups from Procurement/Contracts before we share with our external counsel: 

- Orbis agrees with the 10 business day snapshot window and the 7 business day artifact turnaround; can you add explicit language about business-day definition and timezone (we operate PT).
- We need a clause that allows an emergency production access window for incident response with a maximum of 2-hour operator session notification during a declared incident. That operator session must be auditable and constrained; suggest language for incident-only ephemeral access.
- Please confirm whether Redwood will accept an independent, mutually agreed forensic auditor (one per audit) and the financial responsibility split for auditor fees when the audit is not tied to a breach.

If you can accept the above edits we will push to our counsel and aim to return redlines in 3 business days. Also include the DocuSign link that you prefer for the addendum final signature.

Thanks,
